mappiq.title: Mappiq
mappiq.definition: A dot in a final ה that indicates the consonant is pronounced (not silent). Often discussed in forms like בָּהּ (bah, ‘in her’).

dagesh.title: Dagesh
dagesh.definition: A dot placed inside a Hebrew consonant. Depending on context it can mark hardening (dagesh qal/lene) or doubling/gemination (dagesh chazaq/forte).

sheva.title: Sheva
sheva.definition: Two vertical dots under a consonant. Can be vocal (very short vowel) or silent (no vowel), depending on position and phonological context.

niqqud.title: Niqqud
niqqud.definition: The Hebrew vowel-pointing system added by the Masoretes to preserve pronunciation without changing the consonantal text.

chataf.title: Chataf
chataf.definition: A reduced (‘ultra-short’) vowel sign used primarily with guttural letters (e.g., chataf patach, chataf segol, chataf qamats).

qamats qatan.title: Qamats Qatan
qamats qatan.definition: A short ‘o’ value of qamats that appears in specific closed, unaccented syllable environments.

shemot.title: Shemot
shemot.definition: Plural of shem (name). In grammar context: ‘nouns’/‘names,’ often used as a label category in Hebrew instruction.

be-.title: be-
be-.definition: Inseparable preposition prefix meaning ‘in, with, by’. Often attached directly to the following noun.

le-.title: le-
le-.definition: Inseparable preposition prefix meaning ‘to, for’. Often attached directly to the following noun.

min-.title: min-
min-.definition: Preposition meaning ‘from’. Commonly assimilates/shortens to מִ or מֵ depending on the following letter.

ha-.title: ha-
ha-.definition: Definite article prefix meaning 'the'. It attaches to a noun and often triggers predictable vowel/dagesh changes.

ve-.title: ve-
ve-.definition: Conjunction prefix meaning 'and'. Often attached directly to the following word.
